tests.description: Timed check on Greek Warfare & the Hoplite Phalanx

questions.question: Q: How did the hoplite phalanx work as a fighting formation?
questions.correctAnswer: Hoplites stood in close ranks, typically 8 men deep, with shields overlapping on the left. Each man's shield protected his neighbour's exposed right side. Spears projected forward over the shield wall. The formation advanced as a solid mass, pushing against the enemy phalanx (othismos). Breaking the enemy line usually decided the battle.

questions.question: Q: Why did the rise of the Athenian navy increase democracy?
questions.correctAnswer: Athens' navy required thousands of rowers (thetes, the poorest citizens). Since thetes were essential for Athens' military power, their political influence grew. Pericles introduced pay for public service partly because thetes who rowed in the fleet demanded political rights commensurate with their military contribution.

questions.question: Q: What was a trireme and how was it used in battle?
questions.correctAnswer: A trireme was a fast, manoeuvrable warship with three banks of oars (about 170 rowers) and a bronze ram at the prow. In battle, triremes tried to ram enemy ships, rowing at speed to hole their hulls, or to shear off their oars by rowing past closely.

tests.description: Short-answer practice on Greek Warfare & the Hoplite Phalanx

questions.question: Q: What equipment did a hoplite carry and who provided it?
questions.correctAnswer: Each hoplite provided his own equipment: aspis (large round shield), dory (spear), xiphos (short sword), Corinthian helmet, bronze cuirass (breastplate) and greaves (shin guards). This meant only citizens wealthy enough to afford the equipment could serve as hoplites.

questions.question: Q: Why was the right wing of a phalanx so important?
questions.correctAnswer: Each hoplite's shield covered his left side and his neighbour's right side, so the right side of each soldier was exposed. Phalanxes therefore drifted rightward as soldiers sought the protection of the man to their right. The right wing was the position of honour and typically held the best troops.
